subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What measurement environment and acceptance bar should define the native Linux VPS reasoning-latency analysis?
rationale: The request spans gateway runtime, context assembly, memory search, compaction, subagents, hooks, auth, Telegram delivery, and host constraints, so automation should not invent scope or target hardware.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a maintainer-scoped native-Linux VPS runbook that uses existing diagnostics and identifies which missing spans or metrics need follow-up.

options.title: Add missing spans first
options.body: Prioritize instrumentation gaps such as bundle MCP and embedded prep details before writing the broader latency-analysis document.

options.title: Treat as support only
options.body: Close or defer core work if maintainers do not want a native-VPS performance investigation to become an OpenClaw-owned docs or diagnostics surface.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a maintainer-scoped native-Linux VPS runbook that uses existing diagnostics and identifies which missing spans or metrics need follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Jason is the strongest recent history signal for the observability and docs surfaces that would anchor the runbook.
